correctness.rationale: For points, the k-stage graph is a tree with r blocks; for blocks, the k-stage graph is connected with 1+k(r−1) blocks and cycle rank (k−1)(v−k). The final connected graph has rank (k−1)b−v+1. Each inclusion of graphs injects on integral H1 and the component merges are explicit. This proves all intervals with correct endpoints for all real filtration parameters and all fields. For every design no element is a beat point (r,k≥2); Stong core rigidity and the externally established STS(15) count then yield 80 distinct finite-space homotopy types. The executable independent construction of four designs checks 100 roots and all asserted finite barcodes.

originality.rationale: Badra–Singh arXiv:2610.16386v1 introduces the exact finite-space sublevel filtration and develops the degree-zero theory but does not classify the root-dependent first-homology bars for Steiner incidence posets. The earlier arXiv:2603.18580v1 proves the general downset-cardinality formula without these design-wide persistence calculations. Exact root-dependent first-homology births and the 80 nonhomotopy-equivalent-spaces nonseparation are not consequences of the cited finite-space or independent incidence-Rips/neighborhood-complex classifications without further incidence-graph calculations. The proof supplies this design-dependent calculation. Indexed-source absence cannot establish universal priority.

value.rationale: A natural, recently introduced finite-space filtration receives a complete all-degree and field-independent formula on an infinite family of incidence topologies. The previously degree-zero-focused framework misses the two-stage essential H1 births (k versus k+1). Uniformity across the family exhibits 80 pairwise finite-space-nonhomotopy-equivalent instances with identical complete rooted barcode collections, a substantive limitation on the invariant; neither only numerical recomputation nor arbitrary parameter slicing.
